newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares slide eyeing inflation, and FOCM.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares slide eyeing inflation, and FOCM.

text.p: Italian shares slipped to a lower close on Tuesday with investors eyes focused on a further round of Italian inflation figures later this afternoon and the policy-making FOCM meeting of the Federal Reserve in the U.S., dealers said.

A first round of preliminary inflation data on Monday saw disappointing figures from six Italian cities for September with a further four cities reporting figures today. Concern the FOCM today may raise U.S. interest rates also kept investors on the backfoot, dealers added.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.81 percent at 9,559 and the Mib30 index off 0.86 percent at 14,352.

Preliminary figures on September inflation from six Italian cities came in at 3.4 percent after August's official 3.4 percent and analysts forecast of 3.3 percent, but a Italian Treasury source said late Monday Italian CPI below three percent should still be a "reachable target" by the end of the year.
Concerns over the passage of the 1997 financial budget through parliament also kept investors appetite for the Italian market reserved, dealers said.
Trading was resumed today after a serious breakdown in the software and hardware systems at the bourse's screen-based trading system which blacked out trading for all of Monday.
Among the blue chips, Olivetti was up 0.94 percent at 545.7 lire and Edison, after better than expected first half results late Monday, gained 0.26 percent to 8,820 lire.
But the trend in other top shares was largely down with ENI off 0.81 percent at 7,129 lire, Fiat off 2.43 percent at 4,144 lire and Pirelli down 0.3 percent at 2,635 lire.
